method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, name literal, holder vftable cell, type descriptor name, RTTI name and call target was compared with those listings. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of twelve natives that the earlier contracts do not record: the widget call _addItem, the screen fade natives _fadeIn, _fadeOut, _waitForFading and _fadeInNowLoadingForNoticeEventJustInArea, the actor natives _delete and _getCurrentAreaMaster, the group natives _getMember and _isExistInClientMember, the player query _getBelongGrandCompany, and the NPC background scheduler natives _runBgScheduler and _runBgSchedulerFromMidstream. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists, reads, client state effects, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish fade presentation, group membership, grand company values, scheduler content or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

tierVocabulary.STATIC: Read directly from instructions or data at the cited addresses.
tierVocabulary.INFERRED: A name or role assigned from the surrounding instructions. The bytes do not state it.

framework.reference: manifests/nameplate_group_native_call_contract.json framework, manifests/scheduler_item_native_call_contract.json framework, manifests/spreadsheet_native_call_contract.json framework, manifests/widget_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/talk_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling through 0x00D19A20, the holder receiver adapter, the invalid-parameter route, the return pushers, the world object chain and the yield request.

typeRegistry.order: The constructor stores the StackOperator vftables 0x0110DF38, 0x0110DF60, 0x0110DF88, 0x0110DFB0, 0x0110DFD8, 0x0110E000, 0x0110E028, 0x0110E050, 0x0110E078 and 0x0110E0A0 as entries 0 to 9. Their RTTI names are int, float, bool, Utf8String, LuaControl*, AutoReleaseTentative, Nil, Table, IndividualIndex and Variable.

registration.note: The order of a native is its position among the rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1, as in the scheduler contract. MyPlayer (vftable 0x00FD785C, RTTI .?AVMyPlayer@Control@Client@Script@Lua@Application@@) holds 0x00776340 ('ret 4') in slot 2 and registers nothing.

framework.holdersNote: 0x00726300 (ActorBase) and 0x007265C0 (GroupBase) are recorded in the earlier contracts. The invoke routines cast the receiver with 0x009DA6CC from LuaControl (0x01270B4C) to the target type descriptor. A null cast returns false without calling the callback. The qualifier letter of the holder RTTI name tells const (BEX) from non-const (AEX).

argumentReaders.0x0071BB80: LuaControl* cast to ActorBase, tag 4, recorded in the nameplate contract.
argumentReaders.0x00581AE0: Bounds-tests an index against the cell vector and reads an int.

worldObject.chain: R is the address that 0x00CC7510 returns for ExecuteParameters +0x04. X = [R] and Y = [X +0x04], the chain of the scheduler contract.

fields.Y +0x04: Object whose first dword is the receiver of the identity lookups 0x004D9910 and 0x004D9970. _addItem calls 0x0075B8D0 and 0x0075B900 on it.
fields.Y +0x08: Object whose first dword is V. The fade natives call 0x0075B490, 0x0075B4C0, 0x0075B4F0, 0x0075B510 and 0x0075B500 on it.
fields.Y +0x0C: Dword compared with a group member control by 0x006D02D0.
fields.Y +0x18: Container whose first node holds the control that _getCurrentAreaMaster pushes. The count is at +0x08 of the container.

worldObject.V: V is the dword at the first dword of the objects above. The constructor 0x004DBF40 of Application::Main::RaptureElementContainer (vftable 0x00F912E4) initializes the identity registry at +0x4AC, the log sink pointer at +0x660 and the sheet manager pointer at +0x174F8, the fields the scheduler contract attributes to V, so V is INFERRED to be that container. V +0x17804 is the tree of objects keyed by identity that 0x004D9910 searches. V +0x4CC is the fade object F that 0x004D7340 returns.
worldObject.tier: STATIC for the offsets and calls, INFERRED for the roles.

fadeState.F: Dword at V +0x4CC. 0x005606B0 writes the fourth float at F +0x23C and the byte (frame count > 0 signed) at F +0x244. 0x0055DB00 reads the byte. 0x0055DA80 clears it when its argument is 0x19.
fadeState.scenePacket: 0x004D7980 builds a ScenePacket (vftable 0x00F8CC14) with the type word record number + 0x15. The fade uses record 0, so the type word is 0x15, and a 0x14 byte payload of four floats and the frame count.
fadeState.tier: STATIC for the writes and the packet construction, INFERRED for the roles.

framework.yieldRequest: 0x00CD2860 with ECX set to the Lua thread at ExecuteParameters +0x08 and the checker pointer, as recorded for _wait. Only _waitForFading among these rows calls it.
framework.invalidParameterRoute: A failed cell vector size test, a bounds-tested vector index or a find that returns the head sentinel calls 0x009D22B4. The target cursor contract records that routine as the invalid-parameter route that ends in TerminateProcess.

arguments.note: Control name. A Nil cell selects the variant with an empty name. Any other tag ends the callback without a call.

rows.behavior: Reads three Utf8Strings from the cells 1 to 3, then tests the tag of cell 0. A Utf8String reads cell 0 and calls 0x0075B900 with the receiver identity and the four strings. A Nil cell calls 0x0075B8D0 with the receiver identity and the three strings. Any other tag returns without a call. Both routines look the identity up in the object registry at V +0x17804 and call a widget method on the result without a null test. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The argument list builder declares four entries and every one is registry entry 3, the Utf8String. The first two come from the loop body and the last two through 0x00728480 and 0x007273E0, which select the same entry.
The callback reads cell 1 at 0x006EBC4A, cell 2 at 0x006EBC82 and cell 3 at 0x006EBCBA through 0x0071CE70. Each read follows a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure.

The callback loads the tag byte of cell 0 at 0x006EBCF0 and compares it with 3 and 6. Tag 3 reads the cell through 0x0071CE70 and calls 0x0075B900. Tag 6 calls 0x0075B8D0. Every other tag skips both calls and returns.

0x0075B8D0 and 0x0075B900 pass the first dword of their receiver, the object at Y +0x04, as the receiver of 0x004D9910 with the identity at their first argument, and pass the result as the widget. 0x004D9910 returns the dword at node +0x10 of the tree at +0x17804 of its receiver, keyed by the identity, or 0 when the identity is absent. No instruction tests that result.

0x0075B8D0 forwards the three strings to 0x0053AB60, which pushes the static Utf8String at 0x01266B10 as the name and tail-calls 0x0053AA10. 0x0075B900 calls 0x0053AA10 directly with the first string as the name.

0x0053AA10 compares the name with the static string at 0x01266B10 through 0x00445D20. An equal name uses the dword at widget +0x98. Any other name resolves through 0x005353E0. It then calls 0x00538B70, 0x00537C60 and 0x00535C80 on the widget, runs 0x0053A970 once per entry of the set that 0x00535C80 finds, if any, and ends with 0x00539010 on the widget.

The static string at 0x01266B10 is the empty Utf8String, because the log natives pass it as an empty prefix. The widget at +0x98 is inferred to be the root context. Indexed context lookup, explicit template construction and the Ask list/template/item arguments are scoped by manifests/widget_item_consumer_contract.json. The selected built-in successful-path construction and publication are recorded there. Executed resource/allocation success, registry overrides and lifetime safety remain unqualified.

Whether the declared Utf8String type of argument 0 admits a Nil cell before the callback runs, the complete bodies of 0x00535C80, 0x00539010 and 0x0053A970, and the class of the widget object in the registry. The bounded construction, name/index mapping and property-resolution observations for 0x00538B70 and 0x00537C60 are recorded in manifests/widget_item_consumer_contract.json, with selected built-in successful-path construction and raw name-scope publication. Pre-existing registrations, allocation/resource success and lifetime guarantees remain qualified.

arguments.note: Fade time in seconds. The override multiplies it by 30.0 and truncates it to an int frame count.

rows.behavior: Tail-jumps through slot 0xEC of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase routine is a bare return. The MyPlayer routine converts the seconds to frames, sends a fade to the screen fade object and clears the byte at MyPlayer +0x165. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the three instruction thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0xEC]; jmp eax'. It reads no argument itself.
Slot 0xEC of the PlayerBase vftable (cell 0x00FD5EF0) holds 0x006DE9A0, which is 'ret 4'. Slot 0xEC of the MyPlayer vftable (cell 0x00FD7948) holds 0x006E5CE0.

0x006E5CE0 reads cell 0 as a float through 0x0071BAC0 after a cell vector size test, widens it to a double, multiplies by the double 30.0 at 0x00FA7B18 and truncates with the 32 bit cvttsd2si. It then calls 0x0075B490 with the world object field [Y +0x08] and the frame count, and stores 0 in the byte at the receiver +0x165.
0x0075B490 takes the dword at its receiver as V, calls 0x004D7340 to read the dword F at V +0x4CC and calls 0x005606B0 on F with four 0.0 floats and the frame count.

0x005606B0 copies its four floats and the frame count into a 0x14 byte record and calls 0x004D7980 on F with record number 0, that record and the size 0x14. 0x004D7980 adds 0x15 to the record number, so the ScenePacket (vftable 0x00F8CC14) carries the type word 0x15. After the call 0x005606B0 stores the fourth float at F +0x23C and the byte (frame count > 0 signed) at F +0x244.

The four floats are a target colour and alpha, with the fourth float 0.0 for the fade in and 1.0 for the fade out in 0x0075B4C0. The frame count is seconds times 30.0. The consumer of scene packet type 0x15 was not traced.
The PlayerBase fade slots are no-ops, so a PlayerBase instance that is not a MyPlayer does nothing for this call. Whether the Lua class system creates such instances for other players was not traced.
locators: PlayerBase vftable 0x00FD5E04 holds the no-op 'ret 4' routines 0x006DE9A0, 0x006DE9B0, 0x006DE9C0 and the 'ret 4' routine 0x00776340 in the fade slots. MyPlayer vftable 0x00FD785C is the only class whose RTTI base list names PlayerBase and overrides them.

arguments.note: Fade time in seconds. The override multiplies it by 30.0 and truncates it to an int frame count.

rows.behavior: Tail-jumps through slot 0xF0 of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase routine is a bare return. The MyPlayer routine is the mirror of the _fadeIn override with a fourth float of 1.0, and it stores 1 in the byte at MyPlayer +0x165. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0xF0]; jmp eax'.
Slot 0xF0 of the PlayerBase vftable (cell 0x00FD5EF4) holds 0x006DE9B0, which is 'ret 4'. Slot 0xF0 of the MyPlayer vftable (cell 0x00FD794C) holds 0x006E5D50.
0x006E5D50 repeats the float read, the multiplication by 30.0 and the 32 bit truncation of 0x006E5CE0, calls 0x0075B4C0 and stores 1 in the byte at the receiver +0x165.
0x0075B4C0 differs from 0x0075B490 only in the float list. It passes 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 and 1.0 to 0x005606B0.
The readers of the byte at MyPlayer +0x165 and the consumer of the scene packet were not traced.

rows.behavior: Tail-jumps through slot 0xF4 of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase routine is a bare return. The MyPlayer routine tests the fade flag byte and, when it is set, builds a four byte s_FadeResumeChecker and requests a yield with it. It pushes no value.

facts.claim: The callback is the thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0xF4]; jmp eax'.
Slot 0xF4 of the PlayerBase vftable (cell 0x00FD5EF8) holds 0x006DE9C0, which is 'ret 4'. Slot 0xF4 of the MyPlayer vftable (cell 0x00FD7950) holds 0x006E3160.
0x006E3160 reaches [Y +0x08] through 0x00CC7510 and calls 0x0075B4F0, which reads the byte at F +0x244 through 0x004D7340 and 0x0055DB00. A zero byte returns without a yield.

A nonzero byte allocates 4 bytes through 0x009D1B35, constructs the checker through 0x00716460 and calls 0x00CD2860 with the Lua thread at ExecuteParameters +0x08, the same yield request as _wait. The checker vftable is 0x00FD5628, RTTI name s_FadeResumeChecker in an anonymous namespace, base vftable 0x00FD4F5C. Slot 0 is 0x007164C0, slot 1 is 0x0071C7B0 and slot 2 is 0x00A72A20.

The poll in slot 1 repeats the flag read through [Y +0x08]. A nonzero byte stores the dword at 0x0130CECC, the waiting result, in the result cell and a zero byte stores the dword at 0x01377ECC, the done result.

0x0055DA80 is slot 8 of the vftable 0x00FA4AA8 (RTTI GameManagerElement in Application::Main::Element::System). It clears the byte at its receiver +0x244 when its first argument is 0x19 and clears the byte at +0x245 when it is 0x1A.

F is the GameManagerElement, because it is the only routine group that writes F +0x244 apart from the fade start, and a scene message 0x19 ends the fade. That F is that class and the sender of message 0x19 were not traced.
A fade started with 0 frames stores 0 in the flag, so a following _waitForFading returns at once.

rows.behavior: Tail-jumps through slot 0x108 of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase slot is a bare return. The MyPlayer routine compares the two dwords at MyPlayer +0x128 and +0x12C with the dword 0xE0000000 and, unless both match, calls 0x0075B510 and stores that dword in both fields. It reads no argument, pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0x108]; jmp eax'. Slot 0x108 of the PlayerBase vftable (cell 0x00FD5F0C) holds 0x00776340, which is 'ret 4'. Slot 0x108 of the MyPlayer vftable (cell 0x00FD7964) holds 0x006E32F0.

0x006E32F0 loads the dword at 0x0130C778, which is 0xE0000000. It skips everything when the dwords at the receiver +0x128 and +0x12C both equal it. Otherwise it calls 0x0075B510 with [Y +0x08] and stores the dword in both fields.

0x0075B510 takes the dword at its receiver as V and calls 0x004D70B0 with V and the argument 1. 0x004D70B0 returns when the dword at V +0x175A4 is null. Otherwise it calls 0x004D6820 with -1.0, 0, 0 and 1 and then 0x0056A7C0 on the object at V +0x175A4.

The dwords at MyPlayer +0x128 and +0x12C form an identity pair, and 0xE0000000 is the empty value that group member lookups also return. The routine therefore runs the loading screen fade once per cleared pair.
The writers of MyPlayer +0x128 and +0x12C, the body of 0x004D6820 and the object at V +0x175A4.

rows.behavior: Asks the engine whether the receiver identity is known through 0x00CC7190. A known identity builds a thread context object through 0x00CD2660 and calls slot 0x70 of the receiver vftable. An unknown identity first passes the receiver pointer to 0x00CC7370 and then makes the same slot call. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback loads the engine handle at ExecuteParameters +0x04 and the address of the identity at +0x0C, and calls 0x00CC7190, which tail-calls 0x00CD80F0 on the engine. 0x00CD80F0 tail-calls 0x00D035D0 on the dword at engine +0x1C4.

A nonzero result builds a context object from the Lua thread at ExecuteParameters +0x08 through 0x00CD2660, loads slot 0x70 (index 28) of the receiver vftable and calls it with the engine handle, the identity address and the context.
A zero result calls 0x00CD2660, then 0x00CC7370 with the engine handle and the receiver pointer, then the same slot 0x70 call. 0x00CC7370 calls 0x00CD7A30 and 0x00CDAEB0 on the engine.

Slot 0x70 holds 0x00A72A20, which is 'ret 0xC', in the vftables of ActorBase, CommandDebuggerBase, Math, WidgetHandle, CharaBase, PlayerBase, MyPlayer, NpcBase, GroupBase, ItemBase, WorldMaster, AreaBase, PrivateAreaBase, DirectorBase, Global, DesktopWidget, Debug, DebugBase, CommandBase, StatusBase, JudgeBase, String and Table. Overrides exist in CutScene (0x006E19A0), WidgetBase and DesktopUtil (0x006E3A00), SpreadSheet (0x006E3730), QuestBase (0x006DCFD0) and CommandEventRelationActorBase (0x007187B0).
The SpreadSheet override 0x006E3730 passes the identity to 0x0075BEC0. That routine looks the identity up through 0x004D9910 and, for a found object, calls slot 0 of its vftable with the argument 1.

Slot 0 with the argument 1 is the scalar deleting destructor, so the SpreadSheet override destroys the object registered under the identity. For the classes with the default slot the call has no effect beyond the engine calls above.
The meaning of 0x00CD2660, 0x00CD7A30 and 0x00CDAEB0, what the engine does with an identity it has not seen, and the bodies of the WidgetBase, CutScene and QuestBase overrides.

returns.note: The first element of the list at Y +0x18, or a null control.

rows.behavior: Takes no argument. Reads the container at [Y +0x18]. An empty container pushes a null control through 0x00748B30. Otherwise it pushes the control pointer stored in the first node. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback loads [Y] through 0x00CC7510 and adds 0x18 to it. A zero dword at that address +0x08 pushes a control with the pointer 0 through 0x00748B30.

A nonzero count takes the head sentinel at +0x04 of the container, reads the first node at the sentinel and reads the control pointer at node +0x08. A node equal to the sentinel calls 0x009D22B4. The pointer is pushed through 0x00748B30.

The container is a std::list or std::map shaped tree of area controls with the count at +0x08, so the native returns the first registered area. How the container is filled and whether the first node is the current area were not traced.
Whether the pushed null control reaches Lua as nil, because 0x00748B30 builds the cell through 0x0073DDD0 and the null handling there was not read.

arguments.note: One-based member position. The callback subtracts 1.

returns.note: The control of the member at that position, or a null control.

rows.behavior: Reads an int n and asks the group data at receiver +0x68 for the member identity at index n - 1 through 0x006C0CF0. It resolves the identity to a control through 0x00CC7A50 and pushes the control through 0x00748B30. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 as an int through 0x005819A0 after a cell vector size test, subtracts 1 and calls 0x006C0CF0 on receiver +0x68 with a result slot, the engine handle and the index.

0x006C0CF0 loads the group data pointer at its receiver and calls 0x006C0B80. That routine returns the address 0x0130C778, the dword 0xE0000000, when the byte at group data +0xF6 is zero. Otherwise it indexes the vector of 16 byte entries whose object sits at +0x80, start at +0x84 and end at +0x88, with an unsigned bounds test that calls 0x009D22B4 for an index at or past the count.

An entry whose tag byte at +0x0C is 3 returns the 0xE0000000 address. Other entries are decoded through 0x006CE230 and 0x006CF670 or 0x006CF6A0. The identity is returned only when 0x00CC7A50 resolves it to a control and 0x006D02D0 accepts that control. Otherwise the routine returns the 0xE0000000 address.
0x006D02D0 returns true when the control equals the dword at Y +0x0C and otherwise returns the byte at control +0x5C.

The callback passes the identity to 0x00CC7A50, which asks 0x00CD80F0 whether the engine knows the identity and then calls 0x00CD81D0 or 0x00CD8160. It returns the dword at the found node or 0. The result is pushed through 0x00748B30.
An index at or beyond the member count reaches the invalid-parameter route 0x009D22B4.

The vector at group data +0x84 is the member list, the byte at +0xF6 marks a loaded group, and the second test excludes controls that are neither the local one nor active. The group data class and the entry decoding were not traced.

arguments.handlerRead: 0x0071BB80 tag 4, tag 8 test, 0x00581AE0 for the rest
arguments.note: A member control, an IndividualIndex that always gives false, or a one-based member position.

rows.behavior: Dispatches on the tag of cell 0. A control cell is converted to an identity and tested against the group data at receiver +0x68 through 0x006C3E30. An IndividualIndex pushes false without a lookup. Any other cell is read as an int n and tested as the member position n - 1 through 0x006C3E20. The bool is pushed through 0x00748870. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The argument list builder 0x00742FA0 calls 0x007408C0, which builds a Which through 0x0073E160. That routine declares three alternatives: registry entry 4 (LuaControl*), entry 8 (IndividualIndex) through 0x00728740 and entry 0 (int) through 0x00728740.

The callback loads the tag byte of cell 0 at 0x006FFC3A. Tag 4 reads the cell through 0x0071BB80, converts it to an identity through 0x00CC73B0 and calls 0x006C3E30 on receiver +0x68. Tag 8 stores false. Every other tag reads cell 0 as an int through 0x00581AE0, subtracts 1 and calls 0x006C3E20.

0x006C3E30 and 0x006C3E20 load the group data pointer and jump to 0x006C3B30 and 0x006C3AD0. 0x006C3AD0 indexes the vector of 16 byte entries at group data +0x84 with an unsigned bounds test, calls 0x009D22B4 for an index at or past the count or for a null vector, then calls 0x006D55C0 on the entry and returns the byte it leaves in a local.

For an entry with tag byte 0 at +0x0C, 0x006D55C0 resolves the identity pair at entry +0x08 +4 through 0x00CC7A50, casts the result to ActorBase (type descriptor 0x01270964 from LuaControl 0x01270B4C) through 0x009DA6CC and stores whether the cast succeeded. Another tag takes the branch at 0x006D560A, which was not traced.

0x006C3B30 walks the entries from the vector start at +0x84 to the end at +0x88, compares the identity with the dword at +0x04 of the pointer at entry +0x08 for entries of tag 0 and tag 1 and skips other entries. A match resolves the entry through 0x00CC7A50 and casts it to ActorBase as 0x006D55C0 does. The end of the vector returns false.

The result is true when the member control is registered in the client engine as an actor, which agrees with the name and with the _isExistInWorldMember sibling of the same switchboard. The tag 1 entry layout and the world variant were not traced.
Whether a position outside the member list reaches the invalid-parameter route at run time and what that route does in the process.

returns.note: The sign-extended byte at the receiver +0xED.

rows.behavior: Takes no argument and pushes the sign-extended byte at PlayerBase +0xED as an int. It reads no world state and requests no yield.

arguments.note: Background scheduler name. Its first four bytes are the key.

arguments.handlerRead: 0x0071BA00 when the cell is not Nil
arguments.note: Optional. A true value rebuilds the name from its first three bytes followed by the byte 0x01.

rows.behavior: Reads the name and an optional bool. A true bool replaces the name by its first three bytes plus a byte 1. The first four bytes of the string become a key. The callback creates the key set at NpcBase +0x130 on first use, calls 0x0075C8E0 to start the named scheduler on the receiver chara with start offset 0, and inserts the key into the set when it is absent. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The argument list builder 0x0072D610 declares two entries, registry entry 3 (Utf8String) for the first and entry 2 (bool) for the second.

The callback reads cell 0 through 0x0071CE70 and copies it into a local Utf8String. It then loads the tag byte of cell 1. A Nil tag (6) skips the bool path. Any other tag reads the cell through 0x0071BA00 and the path runs only when the byte is 1.

The bool path copies the first two bytes and the third byte of the string into a four byte buffer, sets the fourth byte to 1 and replaces the string by the NUL terminated buffer through 0x00447260 and 0x00447450.

The key is the dword at the string data pointer that 0x00445210 returns. The callback then loads the engine chain, creates a 0x0C byte tree through 0x00726120 into NpcBase +0x130 when the dword is null and releases the previous object when it differs.

0x0075C8E0 resolves the receiver identity through 0x004D9970 and calls 0x00585320 on the chara with the string data pointer and the offset. 0x00585320 returns 0 when the dword at chara +0xB2C is null. Otherwise it calls 0x00794690 on that object with the address of the key and the offset, then returns 1. The callback ignores the result.
After the call the callback looks the key up in the tree at NpcBase +0x130 through 0x0071D420 and inserts a new entry through 0x00719F70 and 0x006D45A0 when the lookup reaches the end.

The object at chara +0xB2C is the background scheduler runner and the set at NpcBase +0x130 records the keys that were started. The BgSchedulerResumeChecker (vftable 0x00FD5654, poll 0x00716890 on a byte at +0x04) is a different native's waiter. Its relation to the set was not traced.
The body of 0x00794690, the meaning of the byte 1 in the fourth position, the consumers of the set and whether the key names a scheduler by its first four characters.

arguments.note: Background scheduler name. Its first four bytes are the key.
Start offset in seconds. The callback multiplies it by 1000.0.

rows.behavior: Reads the name and a float. The float is multiplied by 1000.0 and truncated to a millisecond count with a 64 bit store. The key, the key set at NpcBase +0x130 and the call to 0x0075C8E0 follow _runBgScheduler, with the millisecond count in place of the offset 0. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The argument list builder 0x0072D710 declares registry entry 3 (Utf8String) and entry 1 (float).

The callback reads cell 0 through 0x0071CE70 and cell 1 through 0x0071BAC0, multiplies the float by the double 1000.0 at 0x00F91C48 on the x87 stack, sets the rounding control to truncate and stores a qword with fistp. The low dword is kept.

The key is the first dword of the string data. The tree at NpcBase +0x130 is created on first use as in _runBgScheduler. 0x0075C8E0 receives the identity address, the string and the millisecond count. Unlike _runBgScheduler there is no bool path and no name rewrite.
The key lookup and the insert into the tree follow the same sequence as in _runBgScheduler.

The millisecond count is the offset into the scheduler at which playback starts, passed through 0x00585320 to 0x00794690 as its second argument. A negative or very large float keeps only the low dword of the 64 bit store.

boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.
Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The run-time order of registration is the switchboard order in the switchboards table of the nameplate contract.
Script call-site counts are static presence in the shipped scripts. They do not establish which natives a given script reaches at run time.
The fade natives are thunks through the receiver vftable. The behavior recorded for them belongs to the MyPlayer override. A PlayerBase receiver that is not a MyPlayer takes the empty base routine.
The consumer of scene packet type 0x15, the sender of the message 0x19 that clears the fade flag and the class of the fade object F were not traced.

manifests/widget_item_consumer_contract.json records bounded widget construction and indexed property resolution behind 0x0053AA10. Its selected built-in path constructs Button Content in ListBoxItem and publishes the named Button. Pre-existing registrations, allocation/resource success and raw name-scope lifetime limits remain. The group data class behind the 16 byte member entries, the writers of the grand company byte and the background scheduler runner behind 0x00794690 were not traced.

The invalid-parameter route ends in a process terminate on the evidence of the target cursor contract. The calls that reach it with an out-of-range member position were not run, so their run-time effect is unknown.
These are client marshalling and state contracts. They do not establish fade presentation, group membership, grand company values, scheduler content or server behavior.
